copy.blurb:
The model fancies Australia more than the market does in this FIFA World Cup 2026 fixture against United States. +9.7pp is a substantive gap; that's what fires this as a Pick on the away side.

Public Elo rates United States 70 points higher than the other side (United States 1810, Australia 1740). The match model's logistic translates that Elo gap directly into a win-probability. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. The adjustment layer is quiet on this fixture — no host bonus, no home-ground correction, no altitude folding in. The Elo numbers above are what the model uses.

Three-way split from the model: United States to win at 44%, the draw at 26%, and Australia to win at 30%. The Desk's three-way distribution is calibrated against the W/D/L resolution Polymarket and Kalshi settle on, not against the exact scoreline. Australia sits at 30% of the mass.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: United States to win at 56%, the draw at 22%, and Australia to win at 20%. Polymarket has Australia at 20%, which prices out at American odds of +400; the model has the same side at 30%. The +9.7pp gap across them is the disagreement we're surfacing.

Pick gate is a lower-bound check, not the point estimate. A 100-sample bootstrap perturbs the Elo prior (±20), the host bonus (±15), and the altitude bonus (±10), then reads the 5th-percentile probability back out. On the Australia side that lower bound is 24% — +4.3pp clear of the market's 20%, comfortably past our +3pp threshold. Calibration tracks the closing market on the bulk sample; selection — picking the single side where the gap is wide — is where the engine's edge has to come from. This verdict is a selection call on the Australia side.

The number above is the most recent read; it isn't frozen. With kickoff 29 days out, we're still on weekly refresh; the daily cadence picks up inside T-5d. Injury news, the actual XI, and weather conditions at kickoff all feed back into the prior when they land. We republish on every refresh. The Desk surfaces edge; what to do with that surface is a reader's call.
drivers: Pre-tournament Elo gives Australia a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +9.7pp gap clears our 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
Calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures, so selection is the lever.
Late-binding signals — form, confirmed XI, weather — re-evaluate closer to kickoff.
copy.summary: This is a Pick on the Australia side — the model has them at 30%, the market at 20%. A +9.7pp gap is enough on a fixture this close to even.
copy.title: United States v Australia · the model leans Australia
